gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Furbo Mini 360° vibrates for 3 seconds to clear a jam (its Treat Toss Helper, on by default), and only HomeGearLab, cited in one chat, sets Furbo's 0.25–0.5 in (0.6–1 cm) round-treat limit against the Petcube Bites 2 Lite's limit of 1 inch or less.
standout_why: I compared VettedFur, TheConsumers.guide, HomeGearLab and our own page. WIRED would not load and PawCog failed on a certificate error. HomeGearLab (cited in the 2026-11-13 chat) already quotes both treat limits: Furbo Mini 360° 'dry, firm, round treats of 0.25 to 0.5 inches' and Petcube 'crunchy treats of 1 inch or less'. It also gives the 2.4 GHz-only Wi-Fi for both. TheConsumers.guide (cited) gives TKENPRO's 7–15 mm range and lists Petcube and the Furbo 360 as 2.4 GHz only. VettedFur gives no treat diameters and says only that 'small pets jam dispensers with the wrong shape'. Our page gives no treat diameter for any product. The only new part is Furbo's own wording on the Mini 360's jam handling (it vibrates to shake treats loose) and its own-treat rule ('smaller than the opening', about 0.6 cm, check against the red box).
decides: Every ChatGPT answer ends by asking 'dog or cat?', and the treat-size limit answers that question. The Furbo Mini 360° launcher takes only small round treats of 0.25–0.5 in, which suits cat treats and small kibble-sized dog treats. The Petcube Bites 2 Lite takes treats up to 1 inch, uniform and ideally round, which suits most dog training treats. So the finding confirms the Petcube as the dog pick and narrows the Mini 360° to small treats. None of the three makers I could read lists 5 GHz, so a home on a 5 GHz-only or band-steered mesh network needs a 2.4 GHz network for the Petcube. This is already covered by cited rivals.
